baseline: entry 8, film 1.0, no-yield Herschel-Bulkley annulus with Erge transition band

smooth.purpose: isolate the turbulent pipe-friction relation without an unmeasured roughness

steel.purpose: illustrative new-steel internal-wall scenario, transferred from EPA water-pipe table; no installed roughness identified

gpds.purpose: NOV GPDS55 catalogue geometry uncertainty, also transferred to insulated pipe; HWDP retained

fh.purpose: conventional FH catalogue geometry uncertainty, also transferred to insulated pipe; HWDP retained

gradual.purpose: idealised zero-local-loss connection limit; other serial component transitions unchanged; not a measured taper

choice_rule: The primary changes only the turbulent friction relation. No joint, roughness or tool coefficient is chosen from pressure or temperature agreement. Catalogue scenarios stay separate until installed equipment records identify a geometry.

tool_uncertainty.reason: No finite published range for the installed HALO, filter, float or sensor loss has been established. Zero additional tool loss is retained and flagged; zero does not imply zero real loss. Different motor examples do not bound these tools.
tool_uncertainty.analogue_use: Context only; reference flow and fluid test conditions are unspecified. They are not installed-tool uncertainty endpoints and are not added to the calculation.

comparison: Score every gap before and after on the frozen samples, with variants separate. G4 is reported even though no transient model changes. The model-only preparation calculates no target residual.
decision_rule: Recommend keeping smooth pipe friction only if its predicted pressure and heat effects are reproduced; G1 assembly-bias RMS worsens by at most 1 psi in either well; G2 absolute well-mean error worsens by at most 0.1 percent of measured mean power; each G3/G6 assembly or group absolute bias and pooled G5 absolute bias worsen by at most 2 C. Report G4 through the unchanged transient treatment. These are acceptance criteria, never parameter choices. Equipment scenarios require an independent installed-equipment source before adoption.

trip_slopes.method_source: validation/model-development/entry-9/analyse.py, slopes; same windows, flow and depth grouping, temperature treatment, mass-rate convention and reductions
outputs: modelled pressure slope in psi per 1000 ft
trip_slopes.eow19: Report separately: the added upper length is insulated pipe. Its connection geometry remains the same declared catalogue transfer as regular pipe.

predictions.baseline: Reproduce entry 9 modelled slopes and ratios.
predictions.smooth: Raise regular and insulated per-length slopes through the pipe-friction relation; it supplies no difference in connection identity.
predictions.steel: Raise the slopes above smooth through the uniform internal roughness example on both regular and insulated pipe.
predictions.gpds: Raise 16B slopes above smooth through smaller catalogue joint bores, including insulated-pipe connections.
predictions.fh: Raise 16B slopes above smooth through smaller conventional FH joint bores, including insulated-pipe connections; expect a larger increment than GPDS55.
predictions.gradual: Reduce the repeated-connection local contribution relative to smooth in regular and insulated pipe. The net sign relative to baseline includes the opposing smooth-friction change.

trip_slopes.selection: Secondary reporting only. It does not enter the unchanged acceptance rule and cannot select any variant or equipment dimension.
